correctness.rationale: For r²=q−k√d≥0, all positive powers of the quadratic conjugates differ, forcing the second irrational root field to equal Q(√d). When odd b≥3 and k odd, r=x+y√d with 2xy=−k forces 2-adic valuations u+v=−1. If u≥0, the j=b summand of the odd coefficient is uniquely 2-adically minimal and negative; if u≤−1, the j=1 summand is. The irrational coefficient cannot equal a negative integer. The b=1, even-b, and divisible-by-four odd-b formulas explicitly construct real bases and nonsquare positive second radicands, proving every implication. Exact rational script checks 58,800 negative-minimum samples and 1,560 constructive cases; tests are supplementary.

originality.rationale: The complete two-shift existence phase diagram cannot be obtained as a special case of the fixed-shift exponent-pair theorem: that theorem assumes n=m in both expressions, whereas the present construction varies the second radicand and gives a sharp condition on m. The 2023 competition solutions likewise fix one shift. Three targeted mathematical-result searches and additional primary-literature keyword searches returned no statement with the same quantifiers. Residual priority from unindexed/implicit algebraic-number-theory arguments is recorded; search absence is not treated as proof of uniqueness.

value.rationale: This is a complete two-parameter existence classification of a natural distinct-radical variant of a newly solved competition question, with a sharp universal congruence obstruction for all odd exponents at least three and constructive contrast for every even exponent. A field-locking principle and exact 2-adic nonintegrality make the phenomenon structural and infinite. It is not merely checking a particular small radicand or numerical cutoff.
